exposure: maternal concentrations of environmental phenols (bisphenols, parabens, benzophenones, triclosan) in early pregnancy
outcome: child behavioral problems (conduct, hyperactivity/inattention, emotion, peer relationship problems)
cohort: The study included 600 mother-child pairs from the Shanghai Birth Cohort.
finding: Maternal levels of specific environmental phenols (2,4-dihydroxy benzophenone (BP1), triclosan (TCS), and methyl 4-hydroxybenzoate (MeP)) during early pregnancy were associated with increased behavioral problems, including hyperactivity/inattention, emotional problems, and peer problems, in 4-year-old children, with stronger positive associations found in boys.
